refutation_attempt: Looked for a copy-before-clear, a self-play guard or shared ownership in Play(Song*), LoadSong and MediaQueue. None: Clear() destroys the owned unique_ptr<Song> before LoadSong reads song->getHandle(), and getQueueProperty()/getActiveSongProperty() expose those raw pointers publicly. XNA's indexer returns fresh wrappers.
reason: Play(Song*) runs queue_.Clear() before LoadSong and PlaySong touch the argument, so passing a queue-owned Song is a heap use-after-free (reads always, writes where SOUND_ENABLED). The call is valid in XNA. Memory-safety on a public path keeps severity high. Orchestrator had independently confirmed it as well.

refutation_attempt: Tried to make previousSong == song possible (LoadSong always allocates a fresh Song, so never), looked for another ActiveSongChanged raise on the collection path (only NextSong/Update set it), and read FNA's handle-comparing Song operator!=, which suppresses the replay event.
reason: Pointer comparison of the queue copy with the caller's Song is always unequal, so replaying the same song raises the event; Play(collection) never sets the flag although the active song changes, contradicting the header's 'Raised when the active song changes'. XNA's native behaviour for the collection case is inferred, not shown by the IL.

refutation_attempt: Looked for copy-back of Duration/PlayCount to the queued copy, or a PlayCount reset on the caller's Song. PlaySong(song) receives the caller's object in Play(Song*) but the queue's copy in Play(collection)/NextSong; Stop() only walks queue_. FNA also never increments PlayCount.
reason: Asymmetry verified in code: Play(Song*) writes Duration and PlayCount to the caller's Song, leaving the queued copy at zero, while the collection and advance paths update the copy. Stop resets only queued copies, and the MediaLibrary.cpp comment about duplicates is wrong for this overload. Low impact.

refutation_attempt: Traced each failure return in PlaySong for a compensating state change, timer reset or Update check (none; ended flag cleared, track destroyed). Checked both mixers' Load paths (empty result vs GetMixer/EnsureMixer throw), Song ctor order after Clear(), and XNA's MediaQueue.Play IL (throws InvalidOperationException).
reason: Re-derived all three paths: a silent return after the old track was destroyed leaves Playing with no track (Update can never advance); a missing device throws raw std::runtime_error after the queue was replaced (SoundEffect converts it); a vanished file throws after Clear(). XNA throws InvalidOperationException. docs/audio-alsa.md documents 'plays nothing', not the stuck state. Medium stands.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a duration copy in LoadSong/PlaySong on the non-SOUND_ENABLED branch, or another source of the queued copy's Duration (probe, mixer). None: LoadSong builds Song(handle, name) and PlaySong sets nothing without a mixer. Verified SOUND_ENABLED is defined only for SDL3 and ALSA.

MEDIA-32 and the header intend elapsed-time end detection when the duration is known, though docs/platform-sdl2.md says MediaPlayer does not play there. Distinct from CNA-BUG-139: other builds, other root cause.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a Video destructor, weak link or ownership that clears video_, and for tests exercising the bad order. None: Video has no destructor, CloseDecoder writes video_->parent_ unconditionally, natural EOF leaves video_ set, Load<Video> proves Video copyable, and every test declares Video before VideoPlayer.
reason: Re-derived: a Video destroyed before its player leaves video_ dangling; Stop, Dispose or the destructor then writes video_->parent_ into freed memory, and a copied playing Video keeps a stale parent_. XNA/FNA are garbage-collected, and the headers state no ordering rule. Realistic via member order or UnloadContent; medium stands.

Decoder throw sites and OpenDecoder's close-and-rethrow verified.

Throwing itself matches XNA and Play's exception type is test-pinned, so the defect is the undocumented type and undefined post-state.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a seek, flush or pending-packet reset on the switch path in VideoPlayer::SetVideoTrackEXT and OpenVideoStreamByIndex (none; SeekToStart is the only place that clears havePendingVideoPacket_), and for a two-video-stream fixture or test (none). Decoder outcome per codec is inferred.
reason: A genuine mid-playback switch frees the codec context and opens a fresh one at the demuxer's current position, without seek or pending-packet reset; CNA's own comment explains the non-keyframe failure. The class of files (two video streams, inter-coded) and codec behaviour are unexecuted, so strong inference. Low severity fits.

refutation_attempt: Searched the decoder for any read of color_range/colorspace or a swscale path (none), modelled the formula in Python (black 16,16,16; white 235), and ffprobed the fixtures: all are tv-range bt470bg, so limited-range bars decode up to 17 off yet pass the +/-20 tests.
reason: Converter is hard-wired full-range BT.601 and is applied to limited-range yuv420p/422p/444p, 10/12-bit and NV12 alike, so ordinary H.264/VP9/AV1 video shows lifted blacks and reduced contrast, BT.709 gets wrong hue. This hits most real video, so severity should be medium, not low. Fixtures are tv-range, which the entry did not check.

refutation_attempt: Checked whether the cut is deliberate (plan D6 and a pinning test say yes), whether Cue destruction really stops sound (Cue::~Cue runs Dispose then StopInternal), and FNA's PlayCue (null cue handed to FAudio, no age cap). Looked for a CHECKLIST accepted deviation: none.
reason: A looping or paused PlayCue cue reaches the 5-minute net, AudioEngine::Update or the next PlayCue erases it, and Cue's destructor stops the sound. XNA/FAudio impose no cap. It is a deliberate plan decision (D6), but that contradicts XNA and CNA's own 'never affects ordinary playback' comment. Medium stands.

refutation_attempt: XNA IL matches (ArgumentException for empty, unaligned, non-positive count). But I found three tests pinning no-throw for a 63-byte buffer and an odd float count (plan P9-DYNAMIC-009, 'matches FNA'), and both mixers' PutMixerStreamData: SDL3 rejects partial frames, so 'shifts every later sample' fails there.
reason: Missing validation is real and CLAUDE.md makes XNA win over FNA. But three tests pin the no-throw behaviour (contrary to 'no test submits an unaligned buffer'), and the consequence is backend-specific: SDL3 audio drops the chunk with a stderr diagnostic, only CNA's ALSA mixer plays shifted audio.

correction.summary: CNA checks only that offset and count lie inside the buffer; XNA throws ArgumentException for an empty buffer, a length, offset or count that is not block-aligned, or a count of zero. Such submissions are queued without error, then dropped by SDL3 audio or played shifted by CNA's ALSA mixer. SubmitFloatBufferEXT (an FNA extension with no XNA contract) has the same gap for channel frames.
correction.actual: SubmitBuffer in modules/audio/src/Xna/DynamicSoundEffectInstance.cpp throws only when the instance is disposed, when offset/count are negative or overrun the buffer, or on the int/float mode guard; an empty buffer, a zero count and a byte count that is not a whole number of frames are queued without an error. What happens next depends on the mixer. With SDL3 audio, SDL_PutAudioStreamData refuses a chunk that is not a whole number of frames ("Can't add partial sample frames"), so SubmitQueuedToStreamLocked writes "stream submit failed (N bytes dropped)" to stderr and the chunk is silently lost. With CNA's own ALSA mixer, PutMixerStreamData appends the bytes unchecked and ReadFrame consumes whole frames, so a partial frame at the end of one chunk joins the start of the next and shifts every later sample (stereo channels swap, 16-bit samples split).
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading at 009d40f5 against the XNA 4.0 IL of DynamicSoundEffectInstance.SubmitBuffer; not executed. Three tests pin the current no-throw behaviour on purpose (SubmitBufferWithNonFrameAlignedByteCountDoesNotThrowWhileStopped, SubmitBufferWithNonFrameAlignedByteCountWhilePlayingDoesNotThrow, SubmitFloatBufferWithSampleCountNotDivisibleByChannelCountDoesNotThrow, from plan P9-DYNAMIC-009 which matched FNA), so a fix must change them; plans/plan_audio.md records AUD-07-005/006 as open P0 tasks. CNA's own plan records the SDL3 'Can't add partial sample frames' rejection from a real run.

refutation_attempt: Tried to show a violated contract (bug) instead of a gap: CHECKLIST.md rows record the instance-limit collapse, low/high-only filter decode, DSP-preset RPC gap and reverb no-op as accepted FAudio-parity deviations, and XACT is native, not IL. Checked each code claim; RPC numbering was mislabelled.
reason: Class is right: each item is a documented, deliberate FAudio-parity limitation (CHECKLIST.md), not a contract violation. One detail is wrong: Cue::EvaluateRpc handles parameters 0, 1, 3 and 4, so the reverb-send target is parameter 2 (also ignored), while DSP presets are 5 and above.

correction.actual: CheckCategoryInstanceLimit and CheckCueInstanceLimit in modules/audio/src/Xna/AudioEngine.cpp treat QUEUE and REPLACE_QUIETEST as REPLACE_OLDEST and, for a cue-level limit, search every live cue of the bank for the victim, matching FAudio's handle_instance_limit (whose own source carries a FIXME). modules/audio/src/Internal/XactParser.cpp decodes the filter type with FAudio's (filterData >> 1) & 0x02, which can yield only low- or high-pass. Cue::EvaluateRpc in modules/audio/src/Xna/Cue.cpp applies RPC targets 0 (volume), 1 (pitch), 3 (filter frequency) and 4 (filter Q) only: the reverb-send target (parameter 2) and every DSP-preset target (parameter 5 and above) are parsed but never applied, and SoundEffectInstance::INTERNAL_applyReverb is a documented no-op because the mixer has no aux-send bus. CHECKLIST.md records the instance-limit collapse, the low/high-only filter decode, the DSP-preset RPC gap and the reverb no-op as accepted deviations, and plans/plan_audio20260717.md (P10-RPC-001) records the unapplied reverb-send RPC target.

refutation_attempt: Recounted TEST definitions (all exact), re-read the UnitTests.cmake exclusions and the CI gtest filter, then hunted for ALSA-run suites that play cues: AudioCategoryTests keeps 12 cue-playing cases, contradicting 'Cue/SoundBank/WaveBank playback not exercised'. The CI filter also skips CnaMixerXnaRecording.

The CI filter omits the recording case (ctest-only), and the ALSA cell builds no media tests. Dedicated Cue/SoundBank/WaveBank suites remain SDL3-only.

correction.title: The XNA audio facade on CNA's own ALSA mixer is covered by seven facade tests plus the XACT category suite; the SoundEffect, instance, dynamic-instance, Cue, SoundBank and WaveBank suites run only on SDL3
correction.summary: Under CNA_AUDIO_PLATFORM=ALSA, eight SDL3_mixer-bound suites (about 440 test definitions) are filtered out, so SoundEffect, SoundEffectInstance and DynamicSoundEffectInstance behaviour on CNA's mixer rests on seven facade cases, and Cue, SoundBank and WaveBank playback on the twelve AudioCategoryTests cases that play cues from real banks.
correction.actual:
cmake/UnitTests.cmake removes those eight suites from CnaTests for every non-SDL3 audio selection, because they read SDL3_mixer's own track handles. For ALSA it keeps AudioCategoryTests. What exercises the XNA facade on CNA's mixer is therefore modules/audio/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Audio/CnaMixerXnaTests.cpp (seven cases: a fire-and-forget play, an instance playing for its duration, pause/resume/stop, a looped instance, a dynamic instance consuming buffers, which file formats load, and one end-to-end recording through ALSA's file device), modules/audio/tests/CNA/Internal/Audio/CnaMixerTests.cpp (24 mixer-level cases), AudioCategoryTests (28 cases, twelve of which play cues from real SoundBank fixtures, nine with WaveBank-backed instances, and check pause, resume, stop, volume and instance-limit eviction through the public API), the microphone suites and one ALSA-only MediaPlayer song-end case. Not exercised on ALSA: Apply3D and the pan crossfeed, pitch, authored loop regions, the 3D-versus-pan gate, instance state edge cases, the behaviour the dedicated CueTests, SoundBankTests and WaveBankTests pin (RPC curves, variations, wave formats, streaming reads, fire-and-forget sweeping) and the offline renderer.
The X11 + ALSA cell of .github/workflows/platform-ci.yml builds only CnaAudioTests and runs a filtered selection on ALSA's silent null device. The filter (CnaMixer.*, CnaMixerXna.*, AlsaAudioDevice.*, AlsaAudioRecordingDevice.*, Microphone*, AudioCategory*, *AudioDeviceConformanceTests*, AudioEngine*, RendererDetail*) does not match the CnaMixerXnaRecording suite, so the recording case runs only under ctest's CnaAudioAlsaRecordingTest, and the ALSA-only MediaPlayer case lives in the media test binary that this cell does not build. No lane plays to a physical sound card.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading at 009d40f5; no test was run. Test counts are TEST/TEST_F/TEST_P definitions counted in the source files, not executed cases (133, 92, 61, 57, 38, 36, 17 and 8 for the eight excluded suites, 7 for CnaMixerXnaTests, 24 for CnaMixerTests, 28 for AudioCategoryTests). Nothing is known to be wrong on the ALSA mixer; the gap is the missing evidence.

correction.title: Media paths without tests: the natural song end on SDL3_mixer, the failed visualization install, MediaLibrary accessors after Dispose and SavePicture's IOException
correction.actual:
Natural song end on SDL3_mixer. OnMusicTrackStopped sets the ended flag from the audio thread and Update advances, stops or repeats. The only test that lets a song finish, MediaPlayerTest.Mp3AndFlacSongsPlayThroughCnasOwnMixerToTheirEnd, is compiled only for ALSA audio.
Visualization without a tap. The comment on VisualizationEnabledStateStaysConsistentWithGetVisualizationData states that the suite always has a dummy SDL device, so the no-mixer and failed-install branches of setIsVisualizationEnabledProperty are correct by construction only.
MediaLibrary::Dispose. It only sets isDisposed_; the collection accessors do not consult it. MediaLibraryTestFixture.DisposeMarksLibraryDisposed checks the flag and nothing else; the pure-C CApi_MediaLibrarySmoke additionally pins a repeated dispose and that cna_media_library_get_songs still succeeds on a disposed library, but no test pins the other accessors.
SavePicture failure. MediaLibrary::SavePicture throws System::IO::IOException when the store returns no path. The store's name-sanitising and empty-root cases are tested at store level (SavedPictureStoreTests.cpp), but no test drives the public method into the exception.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading the test sources at 009d40f5; no test was run. Nothing in these paths is known to be wrong; the gap is evidence. The pure-C smoke tests under modules/c-api/tests/pure_c are registered with ctest (CApi_MediaLibrarySmoke, CApi_MediaPlayerSmoke) and were not counted by the entry; they do not let a song finish or drive SavePicture to an IOException. MediaLibrary::Dispose not guarding its accessors is recorded as observed, not judged against XNA here.
